title: Remark
body_md: Although \eqref{C} and local uniform convergence are not equivalent, it will follow directly from the proofs of Theorems \ref{thm:main1} and \ref{thm:main2} that the constructed mean curvature flows will satisfy $\mathcal{M}_{t} \to \mathcal{M}_{0}$ locally uniformly in $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ as $t \to 0$.
head: environment

label: thm:main1
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:main1}
    Let $\mathcal{M}_{0}$ be either a \emph{raindrop} or a \emph{UFO} hypersurface in $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$.
                                                                                                                                                            
    Then there exists a smooth mean curvature flow
    \[
        F:S^{n} \times (0,T)\to\mathbb{R}^{n+1},
    \]
    such that $\mathcal{M}_t$ converges to $\mathcal{M}_0$ as $t\to0$ in the sense of \eqref{C} and $\mathcal{M}_{t}$ converges to a point on the $x$-axis as $t \to T$. Additionally, $\tfrac{h^2}{2n}\leq T\leq\tfrac{A_0}{2\pi}$, where $h$ is the radius of a sphere enclosed by the initial condition and $A_0$ is the area enclosed by the profile curve of the initial condition (see also Definitions \eqref{def:raindropIC} and \eqref{def:UFOIC} for $h$ and $A_0$).
head: environment

label: thm:main2
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:main2}
    Let $\mathcal{M}_{0}$ be a \emph{stretched torus} hypersurface in $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$. 
    Then there exists a smooth mean curvature flow
    \[
        F:S^1\times S^{n-1} \times (0,T) \to \mathbb{R}^{n+1},
    \]
    such that $\mathcal{M}_t$ converges to $\mathcal{M}_0$ as $t\to0$ in the sense of \eqref{C}. Additionally, $T\geq\min\{\tfrac{h^2}{2n},\tfrac{\ell^2}{2(n-1)}\}$, where $h$ is the radius of a sphere enclosed by the initial condition and $\ell$ is the distance between $\mathcal{M}_0$ and the axis of rotation (see also Definition \ref{def:stretchedtorusIC} for $h$ and $\ell$).
head: environment

title: Definition
head: environment

title: Definition
body_md:
Let $F_{0}:M^{n} \to \mathbb{R}^{n+1}$, be a smooth immersion of an $n$-dimensional manifold without boundary $M^{n}$. Then we say that a one-parameter family of smooth immersions $F:M^{n} \times [0,T) \to \mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ is a mean curvature flow with initial data $F_{0}$, if 
    \[
        \begin{cases}
            \displaystyle\frac{\partial F}{\partial t}(x,t) = \vec{H}(x,t) & (x,t) \in M^{n} \times [0,T) \\
            F(x,0) = F_{0}(x) & x \in M^{n}.
        \end{cases}
    \]
    where $\vec{H}(x,t)$ is the mean curvature vector of the immersion $F(x,t)$.

label: thm:point
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:point}
    If $\Gamma_{0}$ can be globally expressed as a horizontal graph $u(x)$ with one global maximum and no other interior critical points, then the family of hypersurfaces $\{\Sigma_{t}\}_{t \in [0,T)}$  converges to a point on the $x$-axis as $t \to T$.
head: environment

label: thm:horizontal_gradient
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:horizontal_gradient}
If $\Gamma_{0}$ can be globally expressed as the graph of a function $r = u(x)$ over the $x$-axis, then so can the profile curves $\Gamma_{t}$ of $\Sigma_{t}$ for each $t \in [0,T)$. Furthermore, if we denote the corresponding solution to the horizontal graph equation \eqref{eq:horizontal_graph_equation} by $r = u(x,t)$ where $u:[\alpha(t),\beta(t)] \times [0,T) \to \mathbb{R}$, then there is a function $\sigma:\mathbb{R}_{+} \times \mathbb{R}_{+} \to \mathbb{R}$ such that 
\[
    |u_{x}(x,t)| \leq \sigma(u(x,t),t),
\]
for all $0 < t < T$, where $\sigma(u,t)$ is non-increasing in both variables and depends only on $\sup_{x \in (\alpha(0),\beta(0))}u(x,0)$.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md: In \cite{AltschulerAngenentGiga1995} it is shown that the estimate in Theorem \ref{thm:horizontal_gradient} holds with $\sigma(u,t) = e^{\rho(u)/t}$ where $\rho(u)$ is a positive non-increasing function on $\mathbb{R}_{+}$ such that $\rho \overset{u \to 0}{\longrightarrow} \infty$.
head: environment

label: thm:evans_spruck
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:evans_spruck}
    If $w \in C^{3}(\overline{\Omega}_{T}) \cap C(\Omega_{T})$ is a solution to the full graph equation \eqref{eq:full_graph_equation} in a domain $\Omega_{T} \doteqdot B_{r}(p) \times (0,T)$, then for all $\epsilon > 0$ there exists a constant $C \doteqdot C(\sup|w|,\epsilon,n,r)$ for which
    \[
        |\nabla w| \leq C
    \]
    in $B_{r-\epsilon}(p) \times (\epsilon^{2},T)$.
head: environment

label: def:raindropIC
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:raindropIC}
    Consider a smooth function over the $x$-axis \begin{equation*}
        u:[-a,\infty)\to[0,b],
    \end{equation*} where $2a\geq b>0$, that satisfies the following: 
    \begin{itemize}
        \item[(i)] The graph of $u$ meets the $x$-axis orthogonally at $x = -a$, and the region bounded by the graph of $u$ and the $x$-axis has finite area equal to $\tfrac{A_0}{2}$.
        \item[(ii)] $u$ is monotonically increasing on $(-a,0)$ and monotonically decreasing on $(0,\infty)$.
        \item[(iii)] There exists $h\in (0,a)$, such that the semi-circle $\{(x, \sqrt{h^2-x^2}):x\in[-h,h]\}$ lies strictly under the graph of $u$.
    \end{itemize}
    We will denote the graph of $u$ by 
    \[
        \mathfrak{R} \doteqdot \text{\emph{graph}}(u),
    \]
    and refer to the surface $\mathcal{R}$ obtained by rotating $\mathfrak{R}$ about the $x$-axis as a \emph{raindrop hypersurface} (see Figure \ref{fig:RD_UFO_ICs}).
head: environment
name: Raindrop

label: def:UFOIC
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:UFOIC}
    Consider a smooth function over the $r$-axis $$v:[0,\infty)\to[0,d],$$ where $d>0$, that satisfies the following: \begin{itemize}
        \item[(i)] The graph of $v$ meets the $x$-axis orthogonally and the region bounded by the graph of $v$, the $r$-axis and the $x$-axis has finite area equal to $\tfrac{A_0}{4}$.
        \item[(ii)] $v$ is monotonically decreasing on $(0,\infty)$.
        \item[(iii)] There exists $h \in (0,d)$ such that the semi-circle $\{(x, \sqrt{h^2-x^2}):x\in[-h,h]\}$ lies strictly under by the graphs of $v$ and $-v$.
    \end{itemize}
    We will denote the union of the graphs of $v$ and $-v$ by 
    \[
        \mathfrak{U} \doteqdot \text{\emph{graph}}(v) \cup \text{\emph{graph}}(-v)
    \]
    and refer to the surface $\mathcal{U}$ obtained by rotating $\mathfrak{U}$ about the $x$-axis as a \emph{UFO hypersurface} (see again Figure \ref{fig:RD_UFO_ICs}).
head: environment
name: UFO

label: def:stretchedtorusIC
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:stretchedtorusIC}
    Consider a smooth function over the $r$-axis $$v:[\ell,\infty)\to[0,L],$$ where $\ell,L>0$, that satisfies the following: \begin{itemize}
        \item[(i)] $v$ meets the $r$-axis orthogonally and the region bounded by the graph of $v$ and the $r$-axis has finite area.
        \item[(ii)] There exists $C>\ell>0$ and $h>\tfrac{L}{2}>0$ such that $x=\sqrt{h^2-(y-C)^2}$ is strictly contained by the graph of $v$ and the $r$-axis.
        \item[(iii)] $v$ is monotonically increasing on $(\ell,C)$ and monotonically decreasing on $(C,\infty)$.
    \end{itemize}
    We will denote the union of the graphs of $v$ and $-v$ by 
    \[
        \mathfrak{T} \doteqdot \text{\emph{graph}}(v) \cup \text{\emph{graph}}(-v)
    \]
    and refer to the surface $\mathcal{T}$ obtained by rotating $\mathfrak{T}$ about the $x$-axis as a \emph{stretched torus hypersurface}.

name: Stretched Torus

name: Compact Slings

title: Definition
body_md: We shall refer to the maximal family of hypersurfaces obtained by evolving a compact sling under the mean curvature flow as a \emph{slingshot}. If $\mathcal{R}^{j}$, $\mathcal{U}^{j}$ and $\mathcal{T}^{j}$ denotes a compact sling, then we write the corresponding slingshots as $\{\mathcal{R}^{j}_{t}\}_{t \in [0,T_j)}$, $\{\mathcal{U}^{j}_{t}\}_{t \in [0,T_j)}$ and $\{\mathcal{T}^{j}_{t}\}_{t \in [0,T_j)}$, respectively. Similarly, we shall write $\{\mathfrak{R}_{t}^{j}\}_{t \in [0,T_{j})}$, $\{\mathfrak{U}_{t}^{j}\}_{t \in [0,T_{j})}$ and $\{\mathfrak{T}_{t}^{j}\}_{t \in [0,T_{j})}$ for the corresponding evolving families of profile curves.
head: environment

label: lem:compact1
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Any solution to the horizontal graph equation in $n$-dimensions is a sub-solution to the graph equation for curves evolving by curve shortening flow; \begin{equation*}
        u_t=\frac{u_{xx}}{1+u_x^2}-\frac{n-1}{u}\leq\frac{u_{xx}}{1+u_x^2}.
    \end{equation*} Therefore, the solution to the horizontal graph equation in $n$-dimensions will be bounded from above by the solution to the curve shortening flow. 
    
    Consider any raindrop or UFO compact sling $\mathfrak{R}^i_0, \mathfrak{U}_{0}^{i}$ at initial time $t=0$. Let $u^{i}(x,t)$ be the corresponding solution to the horizontal graph equation, and let $\tilde{u}(x,t)$ be the corresponding solution to the graphical curve shortening flow with the same initial data. Since $u^{i}(x,0) = 
    \tilde{u}(x,0)$, the maximum principle implies that $u^{i}(x,t) \leq \tilde{u}(x,t)$ for all $t \in [0,T)$. The result now follows from \cite[Lemma 7]{BourniReiris2024}.
head: environment

label: rem:alt_barrier
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:alt_barrier}
    As an alternative barrier for the raindrop slingshots, one could use the complete graphical solutions defined on the punctured disk constructed in \cite{SaezSchnurer2014}, which in the interior of the disk become finite for any positive time (see Figure 3 in \cite{SaezSchnurer2014}).
head: environment

label: lem:compact2
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: For all stretched tori initial condition $\mathfrak{T}_0$, there exists a UFO initial condition $\mathfrak{U}_0$ which contains it. Therefore, for any $k\in\mathbb{N}$, $\mathfrak{T}_0^k$ is contained inside $\mathfrak{U}_0^{k+1}$. The result then follows by the avoidance principle, together with Lemma \ref{lem:compact1} applied to the flow $\mathfrak{U}^{k+1}_0$.
head: environment

label: prop:curvrain
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The choice $0<t_0<\tfrac{3h^2}{8n}$, together with the avoidance principle, ensures that for all $t\in[0,t_0]$ the interior sphere of $\mathcal{R}_{t}^{k}$ (as given in part (iii) of Definition \ref{def:raindropIC}), has radius greater than $\tfrac{h}{2}$.
    Let $t_{1} \in (0,t_{0})$. By construction,   $\mathcal{R}_{t}^{k}\cap\{r=|y| <\tfrac{h}{2}\}$ has two connected components, each of which can be expressed as the  graph of a function of the form
    \begin{equation*}
        w^k(z_1,\dots,z_n,t)\doteqdot v^k(\sqrt{z_1^2+\cdots+z_n^2},t),
    \end{equation*} 
    where $v^k:[0,\tfrac{h}{2}]\times[t_1,t_0]\to\mathbb{R}_+$ is the corresponding solution to the vertical graph equation. The  profile curves $\mathfrak{R}_{t}^{k}$ do remain vertical graphs in the region ${r < h/2}$ for times $t \le t_0$, and therefore the above representation is well defined. 
    
    To see this, notice that by Theorem \ref{thm:horizontal_gradient}, the profile curve can be written globally via a solution to the horizontal graph equation $u^{k}(x,t)$, which at the initial time has only one critical point, namely the maximum. By Sturm's theorem the number of critical points of $u^k(\cdot,t)$ cannot increase in time.
    Consequently, the evolving profile curve continues to have a unique critical point which is necessarily the maximum, and by our choice of $t_0$, the maximum lies outside the region $r<h/2$. Hence the profile curve remains a vertical graph throughout this region. 
    
    The function $w^k$ is a solution to the full graph equation on $\{y\in\mathbb{R}^n:|y|<\tfrac{h}{2}\}\times[t_1,t_0]$ and
    by Lemma \ref{lem:compact1} is uniformly bounded for all sufficiently large $k$. Therefore, the estimates of Evans-Spruck (Theorem \ref{thm:evans_spruck}) provide uniform, in $k$, bounds on all higher derivatives of $w^k$, which depend only on $h$ and $\sup|w^k|$. 
    
    In the region $\{r > \frac{h}{4}\}$, by construction, the horizontal graph functions $u^k(x,t)$ corresponding to the compact slings $\mathfrak{R}^k_{t}$ satisfy $\sup(u^k(x,0),0)\leq b$ for all $k$. Therefore, by Theorem \ref{thm:horizontal_gradient} there exists some $\sigma:\mathbb{R}^+\times\mathbb{R}^+\to\mathbb{R}^+$ depending only on $b$, for which \begin{equation*}
        |u_x^k(x,t)|\leq\sigma(u^k(x,t),t),
    \end{equation*} for all $k$. Recall that $\sigma$ is non-increasing in its arguments, and therefore, for all $k$, $|u^k_x(x,t)|\le \sigma(\tfrac{h}{4},t_1)$, whenever throughout the region $\{r > \frac{h}{4}\}$ and $t\in [t_1,t_0]$. By the standard regularity theory for parabolic PDE's (see \cite[Chapter III, Theorem 12.1]{LadyzhenskayaSolonnikovUraltseva1968}), we obtain uniform, in $k$, bounds on all higher order derivatives of $u^{k}$. Since the second fundamental form of $\mathcal{R}_{t}^{k}$ can be expressed in terms of the functions $w^{k}$ and $u^{k}$, and their derivatives, we obtain the result.
head: environment

label: prop:curvufo
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
As in the proof of Proposition \ref{prop:curvrain}, our choice of $t_{0} < \frac{3h^{2}}{8n}$ ensures that for each $\mathcal{U}^{k}_{t}$, the interior sphere has radius greater than $\frac{h}{2}$ for all $t \in [0,t_{0}]$ in accordance with the avoidance principle. Let $t_{1} \in (0,t_{0})$. By construction, $\mathcal{U}_{t}^{k} \cap \{r = |y| < \frac{h}{2}\}$ has two connected components, each of which can be expressed as the graph of a function of the form 
    \[
        w^{k}(z_{1},\cdots,z_{n},t) \doteqdot v^{k}(\sqrt{z^{2}_{1} + \cdots + z^{2}_{n},t}),
    \]
    where $v^{k}:[0,\frac{h}{2}] \times [0,t_{0}] \to \mathbb{R}_{+}$ is the corresponding solution to the vertical graph equation. Indeed, the profile curves $\mathfrak{U}_{t}^{k}$ can be globally written via a solution to the horizontal graph equation $u^{k}(x,t)$ by Theorem \ref{thm:horizontal_gradient}, which at the initial time possesses a single critical point, a maximum at $x = 0$. Therefore, arguing as in Proposition \ref{prop:curvrain}, an application of Sturm's theorem implies that the family of profile curves remain a vertical graph throughout the region $\{r < \frac{h}{2}\}$.

    The function $w^{k}$ is a solution to the full graph equation equation on $\{y \in \mathbb{R}^{n}: |y| < \frac{h}{2}\} \times [0,t_{0}]$, and by construction satisfies $w^{k}(x,t) \leq d$. Therefore, the estimates of Evans-Spruck (Theorem \ref{thm:evans_spruck}) provide uniform bounds on the higher derivatives of $w^{k}$, which depend only on $h$ and $d$.

    In the region $\{r > \frac{h}{4}\}$, by Lemma \ref{lem:compact1} there exists a constant $D > 0$ such that the horizontal graph functions $u^{k}(x,t)$ corresponding to the compact slings $\mathfrak{U}_{t}^{k}$ satisfy $\sup u(x,t_{1}) \leq D$ for sufficiently large $k$. Hence, by Theorem \ref{thm:horizontal_gradient}, there exists some 
    $\sigma:\mathbb{R}^{+} \times \mathbb{R}^{+} \to \mathbb{R}^{+}$ depending only on $D$ for which 
    \[
        |u_{x}^{k}(x,t)| \leq \sigma(u^{k}(x,t),t),
    \]
    for all sufficiently large $k$ and $t \in [t_{1},t_{0}]$. Since $\sigma$ is non-increasing in its arguments, we have that 
    $|u^{k}_{x}(x,t)| \leq \sigma\left(\frac{h}{4},t_{1}\right)$ throughout the region $\{r > \frac{h}{4}\}$ for all sufficiently large $k$ and $t \in [t_{1},t_{0}]$. 
    Precisely as in Proposition \ref{prop:curvrain}, after an application of the regularity theory for parabolic PDE's, we obtain the result.
head: environment

label: prop:curvtor
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The choice $t_{0} < (1-\alpha ^2)\min\{\frac{h^{2}}{2n},\frac{\ell^{2}}{2(n-1)}\}$, together with the avoidance principle, ensures that for all $t \in [0,t_{0}]$, the interior sphere of $\mathcal{T}^{k}_{t}$ has radius greater than $\alpha{h}$ and the distance between $\mathcal{T}^{k}_{t}$ and the origin is greater than $\alpha{\ell}$ for all $k$.
    We partition each slingshot $\mathcal{T}_{t}^{k}$ into three regions: the outer region $\{|y| > C + \frac{\alpha h}{2}\}$, the intermediate region $\{C - \alpha h < |y| < C + \alpha h\}$, and the inner region $\{|y| < C - \frac{\alpha h}{2}\}$.

    Arguing as in Propositions \ref{prop:curvrain} and \ref{prop:curvufo}, an application of Sturm's theorem to the corresponding solutions to the horizontal graph equations, $u^{k}_{1}(x,t)$ and $u^{k}_{2}(x,t)$, which lie above and below the regions $\{|y| > C + \alpha h\}$ and $\{|y| < C - \alpha h\}$ respectively, implies that the two components of the profile curves $\mathfrak{T}_{t}^{k}$ remain vertical graphs within the region $\{C-\alpha h < r < C + \alpha h\}$. Therefore, by construction, $\mathcal{T}_{t}^{k} \cap \{C-\alpha h < r < C + \alpha h\}$ has two connected components, each of which can be expressed as the graph of a function of the form 
    \[
        w^{k}(z_{1},\cdots,z_{n},t) \doteqdot v^{k}(\sqrt{z_{1}^{2} + \cdots + z_{n}^{2}},t),
    \]
    where $v^{k}:[C-\alpha h,C+\alpha h] \times [0,t_{0}] \to \mathbb{R}_{+}$ is the corresponding solution to the vertical graph equation. The function $w^{k}$ is a solution to the full graph equation on $\{y \in \mathbb{R}^{n}: C-\alpha h<|y|<C+\alpha h\}$, and by construction satisfies $w^{k}(x,t) \leq L$. Therefore, the estimates of Evans-Spruck (Theorem \ref{thm:evans_spruck}) provide uniform bounds on all the higher order derivatives of $w^{k}$ which depend only on $h, l$ and $L$.

    In the region $\{|y| > C + \frac{\alpha h}{2}\}$, by Theorem \ref{lem:compact2}, there exists a constant $D > 0$ such that the horizontal graph functions $u^{k}_{1}(x,t)$ satisfy $\sup{u(x,t_{1})} \leq D$ for sufficiently large $k$. Hence, by Theorem \ref{thm:horizontal_gradient}, there exists a function $\sigma_{1}:\mathbb{R}_{+} \times \mathbb{R}_{+} \to \mathbb{R}_{+}$ depending only on $D$ for which 
    \[
        |(u_{1}^{k})_{x}(x,t)| \leq \sigma_{1}(u^{k}_{1}(x,t),t),
    \]
    for all sufficiently large $k$ and $t \in [t_{1},t_{0}]$. Therefore, we conclude that $|(u^{k}_{1})_{x}(x,t)| \leq \sigma\left(C+\frac{\alpha h}{2},t_{1}\right)$, throughout the region $\{r > C + \frac{\alpha h}{2}\}$ for all sufficiently large $k$ and $t \in [t_{1},t_{0}]$.

    In the region $\{|y|< C - \frac{\alpha h}{2}\}$, notice that our choice of $t_{0}$ implies that the horizontal graph functions $u^{k}_{2}(x,t)$ satisfy $\alpha\ell \leq u^{k}_{2}(x,t) \leq C - \frac{\alpha h}{2}$ for all $k$ and all $t \in [t_{1},t_{0}]$. Therefore, another application of Theorem \ref{thm:horizontal_gradient} implies the existence of a function $\sigma_{2}:\mathbb{R}_{+} \times \mathbb{R}_{+} \to \mathbb{R}_{+}$ depending only on $C$ and $h$ for which
    \[
        |(u^{k}_{2})_{x}(x,t)| \leq \sigma_{2}(u_{2}^{k}(x,t),t),
    \]
    for all $k$ and $t \in [t_{1},t_{0}]$. Therefore, we conclude that $|(u_{2}^{k})_{x}(x,t)| \leq \sigma_{2}(\alpha\ell,t_{1})$ throughout the region $\{r < C - \frac{\alpha h}{2}\}$ for all $k$ and $t \in [t_{1},t_{0}]$. 

    Precisely as in Propositions \ref{prop:curvrain} and \ref{prop:curvufo}, after an application of the regularity theory for parabolic PDE's, we obtain the result.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We present the proof for the raindrop. The UFO and the stretched torus are proven analogously. 
    
    Let $F^j:S^n\times[0,t_0]\to\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ denote the embedding such that $F^j(S^n,t)=\mathcal{R}^j_{t}$ for any $t\in(0,t_0)$. 
    Because of the estimates in Propositions \ref{prop:curvrain} and \ref{prop:curvufo}, standard compactness arguments (see, e.g., \cite[§11.1.2]{AndrewsChowGuentherLangford2020}) can be applied to extract a convergent subsequence, yielding a smooth mean curvature flow
    \[
        F^{\infty}: S^{n} \times (0,t_{0}] \to \mathbb{R}^{n+1}\,,
    \]
    such that $F^{\infty}(\cdot,t):S^{n} \to \mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ is a hypersurface of revolution for each $t \in (0,t_{0}]$.
    See the proof of Theorem 1 in \cite{BourniReiris2024} for details on the application of the compactness argument in this setting.
    
    The lower bound on this maximal time $T$ is evident from comparison to the sphere $B_h(0)$ contained in $\mathcal{R}_0$. The upper bound on the time of existence is evident from comparing the evolution of the profile curve under the mean curvature flow to its evolution under the curve shortening flow, as in Lemma \ref{lem:compact1}.

    To prove the closeness statement to the initial condition, let $\varepsilon > 0$.  Let $j > 0$ be the smallest number for which $\mathfrak{R}^{k}_0\cap B_{j}(0)^{c}$ is contained in the strip $\{0 \leq r \leq \varepsilon\}$ for all $k > j$. By using balls of radius $\varepsilon > 0$ as barriers, we can ensure that for all $k > j$, $\emptyset \neq \mathfrak{R}^{k}_{t} \cap B_{j}(0)^{c} \subseteq \{0 \leq r \leq \epsilon\}$ for all $t \in [0,\frac{\varepsilon^{2}}{2n}]$. 
    A similar argument using balls of the same radius $\epsilon$ implies that for all $t \in [0,\tfrac{\epsilon^{2}}{2n}]$,
    \[
        \mathcal{R}^{k}_{t} \cap B_{j}(0) \subset B(\mathcal{R}, \varepsilon).
    \]
    Therefore, for all $k > j$ we have 
    \[
        \mathcal{R}^{k}_{t} \subset B(\mathcal{R},\varepsilon)
    \]
    for all $t \in [0,\frac{\epsilon^{2}}{2n}]$, as required.
head: environment
